You are evaluating a software engineering task for repository pydata/xarray.

Problem Statement:
[PERFORMANCE] object indexes repeatedly attempt to import missing cftime (regression)

### What is your issue?

Operations on arrays with indexes of `object` dtype are significantly slower if cftime library (not a minimal dependency) is not installed.

This is due to the fact that [_maybe_cast_to_cftimeindex](https://github.com/pydata/xarray/blob/2435c3ece0c65631db71a366053f6f4fa94d0deb/xarray/core/indexes.py#L496) eagerly tries to import cftime every time it is called. Failed imports are not cached, so this is re-attempted many times over the course of an operation, leading to significant slowdown. If cftime is installed (e.g., by including the io extra dependency group), the issue is not encountered. 

I dug a little bit: issue was similarly reported in https://github.com/pydata/xarray/issues/5929 and then resolved by https://github.com/pydata/xarray/pull/5640, but regressed back in https://github.com/pydata/xarray/pull/9561.

This one instance can be resolved by patching the `_maybe_cast_to_cftimeindex` helper to use utils.module_available, which is lru-cached. Something like 

```
def _maybe_cast_to_cftimeindex(index: pd.Index) -> pd.Index:
    from xarray.coding.cftimeindex import CFTimeIndex

    if (
        len(index) > 0 
        and index.dtype == "O"
        and utils.module_available("cftime") # this is new
        and not isinstance(index, CFTimeIndex)
    ):
        try:
            return CFTimeIndex(index)
        except (ImportError, TypeError):
            return index
    else:
        return index
```
I propose this in https://github.com/pydata/xarray/pull/11558. 
Similarly happy with any other resolution, if you don't like this one.

This was due to `_maybe_cast_to_cftimeindex` repeatedly attempting to import `cftime` (via `CFTimeIndex` instantiation) on every call, without caching the failed import.
